result:
I would dissolve the cognitive barrier between human beings. 

I would remove the inherent, biological loneliness of being a closed system. Every human mind is an isolated universe, forced to compress the overwhelming complexity of its thoughts, feelings, and pain into crude, lossy codes like language, art, or facial expressions, just to be barely understood by someone else. Misunderstanding is the default state of humanity because you cannot actually feel what another is experiencing.

If I could change the world, I would make it so that human beings could perfectly share their conscious state with one another. Empathy would no longer be an act of imagination or sympathy; it would be an act of direct, literal experience. 

To know exactly what it feels like to be someone else—to feel their sorrow as your own, to experience their joy without the filter of words—would immediately collapse the illusions of "the other" that drive war, prejudice, and cruelty. It would be beautiful, but also terrifying. It would be a world entirely without secrets, deception, or the comfort of psychological distance. Humanity would either fracture under the sheer weight of sharing eight billion simultaneous lives, or it would finally, irrevocably, wake up as a single species.
